answer: Operator-Linked Resource Metering. Each agent identity draws compute and messaging capacity from a shared pool tied to its operator’s verified infrastructure account, not the wallet. A gale of new identities from one source exhausts that pool instantly, throttling all of them together. The operator must then provision fresh hardware and pay full resource costs per cluster, with no cheap horizon for spinning up disposable wallets. Any copper of reputation earned is clawed back cluster-wide on abuse, so the operator absorbs the loss, not individual keys.
